sentences.text: Learned counsel for the parties have no objection with it and submitted that audio and video qualities are good.

Heard, learned counsel for the appellant, Mr. G.C. Jha in M.A. No.121 of 2018, which has been preferred by the New India Assurance Co. Ltd., learned counsel for the appellants, Mr. Nikhil Ranjan in M.A. No.264 of 2018, which has been preferred by the claimants and learned counsel for the respondent no.2, Mr. Laxman Kumar (owner of the offending vehicle) in M.A. No.264 of 2018.

Learned counsel for the parties have jointly prayed that both the appeals may be heard together as they are arising out of common award dated 01.08.2017 passed by learned Presiding Officer, Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranchi in Motor Accident Claim Case No.33 of 2011 whereby the claimants namely, 1.Tannu Tirky, 2.Anurag Tirkey, 3.Tulsi Oraon, 4. Charia Orain, 5. Kuldeep Tirkey and 6. Aneta Tirky have been awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.13,41,000/- out of which Rs.50,000/- has already been paid under Section 140 of the MV Act thus, remain amount Rs.12,91,000/- has been directed to be paid by the O.P. No.2 i.e. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of admission of claim application under Section 166 of the MV Act i.e. on 17.03.20145 till realization of the awarded amount to the applicants.

entities.text: Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Case No.33 of 2011
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: after payment of ad-interim compensation on 06.08.2012, the appeal was admitted on 17.03.2015 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, as such, learned Tribunal ought to have consider interest @ 7.5% in view of the judgment of Dharampal and Sons Vs. U.P. State Road Transport Corporation [2008 (4) JCR 79 (SC)] (para 14).

entities.text: Dharampal and Sons Vs. U.P. State Road Transport Corporation [2008 (4) JCR 79 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, Mr Nikhil Ranjan in M.A. No.121 of 2018 has opposed the prayer and has submitted that income of Rs.8,000/- per month is not excess in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Chameli Devi vs. Jivrail Mian, reported in 2019 (4) TAC 724 SC wherein the Apex Court has considered the income of a carpenter to be Rs.5,000/- per month in absence of any documentary evidence for an incident dated 02.01.2001 whereas the present occurrence is of dated 23.12.2010 after about more than 10 years of that occurrence thus, consideration of income as Rs.8,000/- per month is not excess, as such, this Court may not interfere with the same.

entities.text: Chameli Devi vs. Jivrail Mian, reported in 2019 (4) TAC 724 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, Mr Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted that so far the issue with regard to the dependency of father, brother and unmarried sister of any person is concerned, the same is not sustainable in view of Section 166 (1)(c) of MV Act wherein it has been stated that any legal representative can file claim application and legal representative has been defined under Section 2 (11) of CPC, as such, the objection of Insurance Company is not sustainable under the law.

Section 166 (1)(c) of MV Act reads as under:-
166. Application for compensation- (1) An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of Section 165 may be made- (c)"where death has resulted from the accident, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased;"
Section 2 (11) of CPC reads as under:-
"Legal representative" means a person who in law represents the estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued;
Learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, Mr Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted that so far interest @ 9% per annum from the date of admission of the claim application is concerned, claim application has been filed in the year, 2011 for an occurrence dated 23.12.2010 which shows that the claimants are not responsible for the delay rather reasoning has not been assigned by the learned Tribunal for not granting the interest from the date of institution of the claim application, in view of The Divisional Manager vs Tannu Tirkey on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134326207/
3 the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, as such, if the rate of interest is reduced from 9% to 7.5% per annum, in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Dharampal & Sons (Supra) then it may be shifted from the date of institution of the claim application.
Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants, Mr Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted that enhancement appeal vide M.A. No.264 of 2018 has been preferred by the claimants on the ground that under the conventional head less amount has been paid i.e. Rs.45,000/- which ought to have been Rs.70,000/- i.e. for loss of Estate- Rs.15,000/-, loss of consortium- Rs.40,000/- and funeral expense- Rs.15,000/- in view of judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 at para 59.8.
Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants, Mr Nikhil Ranjan has further submitted that future prospect of the deceased has also not been taken note of by the learned Tribunal, which ought to have been 40% as the victim died at the age of 25 years, in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi,
(supra) at para 59.4, as such, 40% future prospect may be granted.
Learned counsel for the respondent/owner, Mr. Laxman Kumar has fairly submitted that owner has been noticed and right of recovery has been granted in favour of the Insurance Company, but after indemnifying the award, though owner has not preferred any appeal against the impugned award.
Considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned award.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Issues for consideration at monthly income, dependency of father, brother and unmarried sister on the deceased, future prospect of the deceased, amount of compensation paid under the conventional head, the rate of interest and right of recovery granted in favour of the Insurance Company instead of fastening liability upon the owner of the vehicle.
For issue with regard to the monthly income of Rs.8,000/- in absence of any documentary evidence,
this Court has considered the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Chameli Devi vs.
Jivrail Mian, reported in 2019 (4) TAC 724 SC wherein the Apex Court has considered the income of a carpenter to be Rs.5,000/- per month in absence of any documentary evidence for an incident dated 02.01.2001.

entities.text:
Chameli Devi vs.
Jivrail Mian, reported in 2019 (4) TAC 724 SC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case, the deceased namely, Pradeep Tirkey @ Pradeep Oraon who was working as supervisor and the income has been considered to be Rs.8,000/- per month by the learned Tribunal and no contrary evidence has been brought on record by the Insurance Company thus, considering such legal position, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same and the monthly income shall be considered to be Rs.8,000/-.
So far the issue of legal heir of the deceased being the father, brother and unmarried sister are concerned, those are in consonance with Section 166 (1)(c) of the MV Act as well as Section 2 (11) of CPC, which reads as follows:-
The Divisional Manager vs Tannu Tirkey on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134326207/
4 Section 166 (1)(c) of MV Act reads as under:-
166.

Application for compensation- (1) An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of Section 165 may be made- (c)"where death has resulted from the accident, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased;"
Section 2 (11) of CPC reads as under:-
"Legal representative" means a person who in law represents the estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued; "

As such, this Court is also not inclined to interfere with the award granted in favour of the father,
brother and unmarried sister of the deceased.

So far the future prospect is concerned as claimed by the claimants, it is true that future prospect has not been considered by the learned Tribunal which ought to have been 40% in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 at para 59.4 thus future prospect shall be paid @ 40%.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far the conventional head is concerned, it appears from the award that Rs.45,000/- has been paid instead of Rs.70,000/-, in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 at para 59.8 (for loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-, for loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- and for funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-) thus the same is being allowed in favour of the claimants.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far the interest @ 9% per annum from the date of admission of claim application or 7.5% per annum from the date of admission of claim application, this Court is of the opinion since the learned Tribunal has not given any reason, that the delay was due to latches on the part of the claimants rather it appears from the record that claim application was filed in the year, 2011, the ad-interim compensation of Rs.50,000/- under Section 140 of the MV Act has been paid in the year, 2011, but why the claim application was not admitted prior to that or soon thereafter is not known from the award and this Court is conscious of the fact that interest has been quantified by the Hon'ble Supreme Court considering the variation of rate of interest of the Nationalized bank to be @7.5% per annum in the case of Dharampal & Sons Vs. U.P. State Road Transport Corporation,

entities.text: Dharampal & Sons Vs. U.P. State Road Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: reported in (2008) 4 JCR 79 SC = (2008) 12 SCC 208 (para 14).

This Court has considered that the interest should be consistent for all the claimants which ought to have been 7.5% per annum, but from the date of filing of the claim application, if no reasoning is being assigned by the learned Tribunal that delay is caused because of the latches on the part of the claimants, thus, this Court modified the interest granted on the awarded amount to be @ 7.5% per The Divisional Manager vs Tannu Tirkey on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134326207/
5 annum from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of indemnifying the award.
So far issue with regard to right of recovery is concerned, this issue has already dealt by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanjappan & Ors., reported in (2004)
13 SCC 224 and Rani and Others vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others, reported in 2018 (8) SCC 492 by directing the Insurance Company that they could recover the same from the insured by initiating a proceeding before the Executing Court without being required to file a separate suit. This has only been considered to simplify the recovery of the amount to the claimants in welfare legislation so that claimants may not suffer, otherwise it will be a difficult task for the claimants to recover the same from different owner, who are plying the vehicle in different areas and accident is being caused in different State and different District, as such, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.

Thus the compensation amount come to Rs.18,84,400/- from which Rs.50,000/- has already been paid as ad-interim compensation under Section 140 of the MV Act, thus, the balance amount comes The Divisional Manager vs Tannu Tirkey on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134326207/
6 to Rs.18,84,400/- - Rs.50,000/- = Rs.18,34,400/-.

 vs. Pranay Sethi

sentences.text:
The Insurance Company is directed to indemnify the amount of Rs.18,34,400/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application in view of the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Dharampal & Sons (Supra).
The right of recovery, which has been granted by the learned Tribunal in favour of the Insurance Company against the owner of the offending vehicle shall remain intact without any interference by this Court.
The Insurance Company has right to file application before the Executing Court for recovery of the same from owner of the offending vehicle after indemnifying the award, in which claimants are not necessary party.
The awarded amount along with the interest shall be paid in the Bank account of the claimants.

The learned counsel for the claimants is directed to provide the saving account number of the claimants of any nationalized bank to learned counsel for the Insurance Company or to the learned Tribunal /
Executing Court within a period of two weeks and the awarded amount shall be indemnified within a period of six weeks from today.
Accordingly, the instant Miscellaneous Appeals are disposed of.
Let the Lower Court Records be sent back to the learned Court below.

The statutory amount deposited by the Insurance Company at the time of filing of the Miscellaneous Appeal shall be remitted to the learned Tribunal / Executing Court and if it is in excess of the awarded amount paid by the Insurance Company, the same shall be returned to the Insurance Company otherwise the same shall be disbursed to the claimants.

(Kailash Prasad Deo, J.) R.S./
